# Tycho strategy brief — 2026-W35

## What changed

Claude Code made sandboxed shell execution the default [clm_100000000001Y3K3MJMKRQPV3X@v1](/claims/clm_100000000001Y3K3MJMKRQPV3X?version=1) and Codex shipped a per-workspace execution sandbox [clm_300000000001YQBZC62ZR10S57@v1](/claims/clm_300000000001YQBZC62ZR10S57?version=1).

## What Tycho concludes

Workspace execution isolation is now a standard control across both monitored vendors rather than an advanced option (likely) [clm_100000000001Y3K3MJMKRQPV3X@v1](/claims/clm_100000000001Y3K3MJMKRQPV3X?version=1)[clm_300000000001YQBZC62ZR10S57@v1](/claims/clm_300000000001YQBZC62ZR10S57?version=1).

## Counter-signals

Both vendors may be answering the same procurement checklist rather than each other. Tycho rejected a second conclusion this period that rested on one vendor's mirrored release text.

## What would change our mind

A subsequent release from either vendor returning execution isolation to an opt-in advanced setting.
